name: Sleep cycle
seoDesc: Sleep cycle: work out ampm from 72 values. A free health calculator with the formula and a worked example.
summary: The Sleep cycle calculator is a free, no-sign-up health tool. Fill in the 6 fields it asks for and it works out waking up time straight away, with the formula shown underneath. It is built for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the Sleep cycle calculator work?
sections.html:
The Sleep cycle calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports waking up time in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the sleeping time); then you type in the figures it asks for.

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

  • Pick the option that matches your case — 96 options, such as 9:00 PM, 9:15 PM and 9:30 PM. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.

sections.title: The formula behind the Sleep cycle calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Waking up time=time to fall asleep + first sleep cycle's length + 5 × next sleep cycles' length + St6
Waking up time=time to fall asleep + first sleep cycle's length + 4 × next sleep cycles' length + St5
Waking up time=time to fall asleep + first sleep cycle's length + 3 × next sleep cycles' length + St4
Waking up time=time to fall asleep + first sleep cycle's length + 2 × next sleep cycles' length + St3
Waking up time=time to fall asleep + first sleep cycle's length + next sleep cycles' length + St2
Waking up time=time to fall asleep + first sleep cycle's length + St1

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Sleep cycle calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

faq.q: What does the Sleep cycle calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns waking up time. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Sleep cycle calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for a few values, which is 6 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (3 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the Sleep cycle calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
